To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat flux is approximately linearly proportional to CH and that CH does not depend strongly on Rb or other surface stability parameters.

the heat flux is approximately linearly related to the product of air sea temperature difference, and wind speed and that the surface bulk Richardson Number is not a useful predictor of the heat flux or the moisture flux.

the sea surface heat flux is linear with respect to the air sea thermal gradient and wind speed and that there are no significant deviations of the sea surface heatflux from this relationship, even in the coastal zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an improved understanding of the sea surface heat flux and its relationship to the air sea thermal structure.
the influence of atmospheric stability on the surface fluxes of momentum, sensible and latent heat and the associated heat fluxes.
the development and application of new methods of remote sensing for the study of the atmosphere ocean system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of the surface stability on the sea surface heat flux is not a dominant factor, at least for the datasets examined here.
the heat flux is generally well described by the linear dependence on the air sea temperature differences and wind speed and that the transfer coefficients are not sensitive to the surface stability.
the stability effect on the surface heat flux is small and not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the influence of stability on the sea surface heat flux is not important, and that the sea surface heat and moisture fluxes can be predicted with a constant transfer coefficient for the open sea and coastal zone.
the heat flux is not significantly influenced by the surface bulk stability.
the heat flux is not linearly related to the surface bulk temperature difference and wind velocity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the open ocean, the heat flux can be predicted with good accuracy by using the bulk formula with a constant heat transfer coefficient.
the heat flux is generally linearly proportional to a product of the air-sea temperature difference and wind velocity, and this relation is valid for a wide range of conditions.
the sea surface temperature is the most important parameter in the heat flux calculation.
